bullets.title: AMD: $5B Anthropic investment + 2GW MI450 chip deal — major AI demand validation
bullets.body: AMD announced a deal to invest up to $5B in Anthropic alongside a purchase commitment from Anthropic for up to 2 gigawatts of AMD's next-gen Instinct MI455X/MI450 chips, with first deliveries beginning H1 2027. The deal, confirmed by WSJ, mirrors NVIDIA's prior Anthropic investment playbook and validates AMD's silicon-agnostic software stack as a credible alternative to NVDA for frontier AI labs. AMD will also use Anthropic's Claude models internally to accelerate chip software development.

bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen Huang rebuts Kimi K3 efficiency narrative; bullish options flow; Vera Rubin ramp
bullets.body: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang argued 'everyone has it backwards' — better AI models drive more compute demand, not less — in direct rebuttal to efficiency-driven bear thesis around Kimi K3. Separately, NVDA showed the most bullish options flow on the day and rallied 2.9% to session highs. Production of Vera racks targeting up to 1,000/day after shipping hundreds of thousands of Grace standalone servers; Vera Rubin pitch is shifting toward token economics as Texas assembly scales.

bullets.title: NVDA: White House accuses Chinese AI startup MoonShot of using banned Blackwell chips via Thailand
bullets.body: The White House alleged Chinese AI startup MoonShot illegally accessed banned NVIDIA Blackwell chips routed through Thailand to build the Kimi K3 model, suggesting ongoing circumvention of US export controls. NVDA's intraday move was attributed in part to these White House comments.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Earnings today after close; capex on track to nearly triple in two years
bullets.body: Alphabet reports earnings after the close with the stock up ~90% YoY; serious volatility is expected. Google's capex is on track to nearly triple within two years, reflecting massive AI infrastructure commitment. Separately, GOOGL flagged as one of three cloud giants (AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL) likely to raise prices amid compute shortage, potentially expanding margins vs. consensus expectations.

bullets.title: TSLA: Reports earnings after close; Musk bull-posting on RoboTaxi; 5% expected move
bullets.body: Tesla reports earnings after the bell with options implying a ~5% move. Musk is publicly bull-posting on the RoboTaxi ahead of results, signaling confidence. One bear-leaning commentator noted TSLA trading below all major moving averages and suggested bearish exposure via TSLQ.

bullets.title: NOW: Reports earnings after close today; Jensen Huang indirectly flagged as bullish
bullets.body: ServiceNow reports after the bell today. One X user noted Jensen Huang's public commentary indirectly signaled a bullish view on NOW. NOW was listed alongside GOOGL and TSLA as the key after-hours events of the session.

bullets.title: GEV: Q revenue $11.1B (+22% YoY) but shares down ~5.6% premarket on wind EBITDA headwinds
bullets.body: GE Vernova reported quarterly revenue of $11.1B, up from $9.1B in the prior-year period, and raised its full-year revenue outlook. Despite the beat and raised guide, shares fell ~5.6% premarket, reversing part of a 65% YTD rally, weighed by wind EBITDA loss concerns.

bullets.title: SMCI: Stock surges 16% — largest single-day gain since June 2022
bullets.body: Super Micro Computer jumped 16% in a single session, its biggest one-day move since June 2022, amid broad AI infrastructure enthusiasm and the broader AI capex narrative driven by OpenAI's raised $750B compute forecast and AMD's Anthropic deal.

bullets.title: CRDO: Strong AI networking fundamentals — next quarter guide $470M, 84–95% YoY growth
bullets.body: Credo Technology positioned as 'the copper king' with a $42.1B market cap; next-quarter guidance of ~$470M represents +7.6% QoQ and +110.7% YoY growth. Four-quarter estimates of $2.45–2.60B imply 84–95% growth with adjusted gross margins of 67–69% and operating margins of 50–53%, described as one of the strongest operating models in its peer group.

bullets.title: AAPL: Plans MacBook and iMac overhaul to meet AI demand; testing MacBook Neo with more RAM
bullets.body: Apple is planning a comprehensive overhaul of its MacBook and iMac product lines driven by AI demand per Bloomberg. The company is also reportedly testing a MacBook Neo variant with increased RAM capacity.

bullets.title: AMD: Zen 6 EPYC Venice — 256-core, 2nm, twin I/O dies entering volume production
bullets.body: AMD's Zen 6 EPYC Venice was pictured as a 256-core processor featuring massive twin I/O dies and is described as the first 2nm HPC chip to enter volume ramp, reinforcing AMD's competitive roadmap against Intel in the data center CPU market.

bullets.title: RDDT/GOOGL: Reddit considering cutting off Google's AI content access
bullets.body: Reddit is reportedly considering restricting Google's access to its content for AI training purposes, signaling Reddit's intent to monetize its proprietary data and reflecting escalating tension over AI training data rights between platforms and AI model developers.

bullets.title: AMZN: Seen as best-positioned hyperscaler to navigate AI buildout; compute shortage to drive price hikes
bullets.body: One credit analyst flagged AMZN as 'almost magical' in its ability to execute the AI infrastructure buildout, while noting that all hyperscalers carry significant tail risk warranting wider spreads. A separate thesis argues AMZN, MSFT, and GOOGL will raise prices in the ongoing compute shortage, potentially delivering margin expansion that the market is not pricing in.

bullets.title: DELL: Trump's March 23 purchase up 253%; stock rallies additional 10% today
bullets.body: President Trump disclosed a purchase of up to $5M of Dell stock on March 23; since that trade, DELL is up 253% and gained an additional 10% on the session. The disclosure context includes Trump promoting Dell from the Oval Office after the purchase.

bullets.title: INTC: Former CEO says bean counters pushing out technologists broke the company
bullets.body: A former Intel CEO, who spent 34 years at the company, attributed Intel's decline to finance-driven leadership displacing technologists, calling Intel 'one of the greatest American companies historically' that went off the rails due to this cultural shift.

bullets.title: CRWV/NBIS: Baird initiates both at Outperform — $100 PT on CRWV, $250 PT on NBIS
bullets.body: Baird initiated coverage on CoreWeave (CRWV) with a $100 price target and Outperform rating, and on Nebius (NBIS) with a $250 price target and Outperform rating, both framed around AI infrastructure demand.

bullets.title: Software/IGV: 'AI Doom trade' hits hard — IGV down ~4% over two sessions
bullets.body: The software sector resumed its selloff with IGV down 2.5% on the day and nearly 4% over two sessions as the 'AI Doom trade' pressures software multiples amid open-model competition and token optimization trends. UBS characterized the AI trade as 'maturing, not breaking.'

bullets.title: CEG/OKLO: Nuclear stocks forming potential technical base after prolonged downtrend
bullets.body: Nuclear power stocks including CEG and OKLO have been in a multi-month downtrend but are 'tightening and coiling,' with one trader watching for bulls to defend support over the next few sessions as a potential technical low forms.

bullets.title: OpenAI raises 2030 capex to $750B; launches $20B Georgia data center — bullish read for AI infra
bullets.body: OpenAI raised its 2030 compute spending forecast to ~$750B (from ~$600B earlier) and announced a $20B data center project (Project Camellia) near Georgia's coast. The upward revision reinforces the AI infrastructure capex supercycle thesis benefiting chip suppliers, power companies, and hyperscalers.

bullets.title: Macro: Fed hike probability hits 36% for July 29 meeting; 30yr TIPS near 3% real yields
bullets.body: Fed funds futures are pricing a 36% probability of a rate hike at the July 29 FOMC meeting. Separately, real yields on 10-year Treasuries hit their highest since 2023, and 30-year TIPS are approaching 3% real yields — the latter described as a potential generational fixed-income buying opportunity. The US 30-year bond yield has traded above 5% for its longest stretch since 2007.
